cases.title: Steady Power Operation
cases.description: Six hundred seconds without a fault should stay close to the reference operating band.

cases.title: Loss Of Feedwater With AFW
cases.eventFamily: NRC SRP 15.2.7 loss of normal feedwater flow
cases.description: Main feedwater trips; auxiliary feedwater starts and should preserve a secondary heat sink.

cases.title: Loss Of Feedwater With Automatic AFW
cases.eventFamily: NRC SRP 15.2.7 loss of normal feedwater flow
cases.description: Main feedwater trips; graph-aware reference I&C should diagnose low-low SG level and actuate AFW without manual schedule help.

cases.title: Loss Of Secondary Heat Sink Without AFW Inventory
cases.eventFamily: NRC SRP Chapter 15 heat-sink degradation envelope
cases.description: Normal feedwater is lost while AFW inventory is unavailable; SG level should uncover tubes and degrade heat transfer in the compact model.

cases.title: Turbine Trip With Steam Bypass
cases.eventFamily: NRC SRP 15.2 turbine trip and loss of load family
cases.description: The turbine path is isolated; electrical load should collapse and main steam bypass/pressure relief behavior should become visible.

cases.title: Pressurizer Overpressure Relief Challenge
cases.eventFamily: NRC SRP 15 reactor coolant system pressure-control challenge
cases.description: An initial high-pressure condition should actuate relief and drive pressure back toward the operating envelope.

cases.title: Steam Generator Tube Leak
cases.eventFamily: NRC SRP 15.6.3 steam generator tube failure indication
cases.description: Primary-to-secondary leakage should drain RCS inventory and produce affected-secondary radiation.

cases.title: Small LOCA With Accumulator Response
cases.description: A primary boundary leak should depressurize, send mass to containment, and actuate passive inventory support.

cases.title: Loss Of Forced Primary Flow
cases.eventFamily: NRC SRP 15.3.1 loss of forced reactor coolant flow
cases.description: All reactor coolant pumps trip; loop flow should coast down, reference protection should trip the reactor, and core cooling indicators should respond.

cases.title: Loss Of Offsite Power
cases.eventFamily: NRC SRP 15.2.6 loss of nonemergency AC power
cases.description: Offsite power is lost; emergency diesels should restore safety buses and essential loads.

results.label: Pressurizer pressure remains in the reference operating band
results.expectation: Stable PWR operation should remain close to nominal RCS pressure.

results.label: Steam-generator level remains controllable
results.expectation: Normal operation should not drift toward dryout or high-level challenge.

results.label: Electric output remains in the reference plant range
results.expectation: The reference plant should produce a plausible large-PWR electrical output at power.

results.label: Loss of feedwater visibly lowers SG level before recovery
results.signal: sgA.levelPercent delta from T+80s to T+170s
results.expectation: Normal feedwater loss should deplete secondary inventory before AFW recovery.

results.label: Auxiliary feedwater reaches the affected SG branch
results.expectation: AFW should provide a visible secondary heat-sink recovery path.

results.label: AFW recovery avoids SG dryout in the demo window
results.expectation: The modeled recovery should preserve a usable heat sink during the scenario.

results.label: Automatic AFW waits for a real low-low level challenge
results.expectation: The automatic response should not mask the initiating loss of feedwater before SG level challenges the low-low setpoint.

results.label: Reference I&C actuates AFW after low-low SG level
results.expectation: Graph-aware steam-generator I&C should open the affected AFW branch without a hand-coded manual schedule.

results.label: Automatic AFW preserves usable SG heat transfer
results.expectation: The affected steam generator should retain a meaningful heat sink after AFW actuation.

results.label: Loss of secondary heat sink uncovers SG tubes
results.expectation: Without AFW inventory, SG level should uncover the tube bundle rather than leaving heat transfer artificially intact.

results.label: Tube uncovering degrades steam-generator heat transfer
results.expectation: The compact SG model should reduce available heat transfer as tubes uncover.

results.label: Loss of heat sink creates a visible core heat-removal deficit
results.expectation: Heat-sink degradation should be visible in core diagnostic terms even in a lumped model.

results.label: Turbine trip rejects generator load
results.expectation: A turbine trip or load rejection should collapse electrical output.

results.label: Turbine stop valve closes
results.expectation: The isolated turbine path should be explicit in the component graph variables.

results.label: Steam bypass opens to absorb the load rejection
results.expectation: A turbine trip should route main steam to the condenser bypass before relying on safety-valve discharge.

results.label: Main steam pressure challenge is visible
results.expectation: The load rejection should produce a detectable main-steam pressure challenge, not only a UI state change.

results.label: Pressurizer relief flow occurs during overpressure challenge
results.expectation: A high RCS-pressure condition should create a visible relief path.

results.label: Pressurizer pressure returns below high-trip challenge band
results.expectation: Relief and normal pressure control should reduce pressure after the overpressure challenge.

results.label: Relief path is visible in primary inventory accounting
results.expectation: Pressurizer relief should be coupled to vessel inventory diagnostics, not only a local pressurizer display variable.

results.label: SGTR produces measurable primary-to-secondary leakage
results.expectation: A tube leak should create an affected-SG leak path without contaminating unrelated SGs.

results.label: SGTR drains primary inventory
results.signal: vessel.primaryCoolantInventoryKg delta from T+80s to final
results.expectation: Primary-to-secondary leakage should produce a durable RCS inventory consequence.

results.label: Affected secondary radiation rises
results.expectation: SGTR diagnosis should be visible through affected secondary radiation.

results.label: Primary boundary leak creates containment release flow
results.expectation: A primary-boundary break should move mass from RCS to containment.

results.label: Containment pressure rises after release
results.signal: containment.pressureMPa delta from T+80s to final
results.expectation: Containment should respond thermodynamically to primary mass-energy release.

results.label: Accumulator injects after depressurization
results.expectation: Passive safety injection should become visible as RCS pressure falls below the accumulator head.

results.label: Forced primary flow coasts down rather than teleporting to zero
results.signal: rcpA.loopFlowKgPerS delta from T+88s to T+110s
results.expectation: RCP trip should show inertia/coastdown, not an instant hydraulic collapse.

results.label: Core cooling availability responds to loss of forced flow
results.expectation: Loss of forced primary flow should be visible in core cooling diagnostics.

results.label: Reference protection suppresses fission power after low-flow trip
results.expectation: Loss of forced primary flow should actuate reactor protection and reduce fission power to a shutdown-range value.

results.label: Reference protection inserts rods after low-flow trip
results.expectation: A low-flow reactor trip should be procedure-visible through rod insertion as well as reduced power.

results.label: Reactor trip isolates turbine load path
results.expectation: The protection response should couple reactor trip, turbine trip, and feedwater isolation behavior.

results.label: Fuel heatup remains bounded in the demo window
results.expectation: The compact model should show bounded thermal consequence during pump coastdown and protection response without claiming severe-accident fidelity.

results.label: Safety bus A recovers after diesel start
results.expectation: LOOP should be visible but recover essential safety bus voltage after EDG start.

results.label: Safety bus B recovers after diesel start
results.expectation: LOOP should be visible but recover redundant safety bus voltage after EDG start.

results.label: Essential plant-control loads remain served after recovery
results.expectation: Emergency power recovery should preserve essential control loads.
